To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

soil pH is the most important soil property regulating the bioavailability of Ni in soil, that soil organic matter is a strong binding ligand for Ni in acidic soils, and that the bioavailability of metals in different soils can vary by more than an order of magnitude.

(1) the bioavailability of nickel in soil is strongly pH dependent; (2) the type of soil has a significant influence on nickel bioavailability and toxicity; and (3) the bioavailable nickel concentration in the soils studied can be estimated with a 0.01M CaCl2 extraction.
soil type (organic matter content) affects the bioavailability of nickel and that the bioavailability of Ni in soils can be predicted with a multi-surface chemical speciation model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of soil composition in regulating metal bioavailability and toxicity.
understanding the effects of soil properties on metal bioavailability.
the development of an understanding on the role of soil characteristics in regulating metal bioavailability, with the aim to improve the assessment of metal bioavailability and risk.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the soil characteristics, including pH, organic matter, clay content, iron (hydr)oxide, and aluminum oxide content, affect metal availability and toxicity, and the effect of each of these characteristics on metal availability is different for different metals.
pH is the most important soil parameter that regulates metal bioavailability and toxicity, but that soil type and other soil parameters can be of additional importance.
soil acidity is the most important soil factor regulating metal bioavailability and toxicity, but that the soil type also plays an important role, especially in acidic soils.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the soil characteristics (pH, organic matter content, clay content and cation exchange capacity) are important factors that affect the bioavailability of metals, and the speciation models are useful tools to understand the mechanisms of metal binding in soil.
soil type and soil pH are both important factors in regulating bioavailability of nickel.
the EC50 values for nickel in soil are not constant, but vary depending on the soil characteristics, especially the soil type.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in order to predict metal bioavailability in soil, one needs to take into account the soil type, as well as the soil pH and metal concentration.
the soil composition and the chemical speciation model can be used to explain differences in metal bioavailability and toxicity among soils.
soil characteristics should be taken into account when assessing bioavailability of metals in soils.
